question: I'm transferring in as a junior with an associate's degree from a NJ community college. Does that mean my general education requirements are already done, or are there Ramapo-specific gen eds I still have to take?
answer:
If your degree is an A.A. or A.S. from a New Jersey community college, the transfer page says you are waived from General Education Requirements once Ramapo receives your final official transcript with the conferred degree. [4,6] The transfer-agreement page also says an A.A. or A.S. fulfills general education requirements for a four-year Ramapo degree. [3]

The pages differ for students transferring with at least 48 credits: the catalog says they must fulfill Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and take one course at Ramapo from each of two distribution categories—Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society. [8,11] If you have at least 48 credits, ask during academic advisement which requirements, if any, remain. [11] The pages do not explain how this 48-credit rule interacts with the A.A./A.S. waiver. [4,8,11]

If your degree is an A.A.S., you are not eligible for a full General Education waiver; courses are evaluated individually. [4]

Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7300. [4] Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7441. [11]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/agreements/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1)

question: how many credits is the history major and how many of those have to be upper level (300/400)?
answer:
The History BA catalog does not publish a total credit count for the major; its requirements list courses only [1]. A separate college policy says major requirements must total at least 40 credits and may not exceed 64 credits, including major-specific concentrations, tracks, and prerequisites [2]. question: Is there a sociology major at Ramapo, and if so what are the required core courses?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo lists Sociology BA, a Bachelor of Arts major. [18] The catalog also lists a Sociology Minor. [1]

Required courses under “Major Requirements” are: [1]
- SOCI 101 INTRODUCTION TO SOCIOLOGY
- SOCI 202 SOCIAL INEQUALITY
- SOCI 215 SOCIOLOGY OF RACE RELATIONS
- SOCI 250 INTERNATIONAL MIGRATION & HUMAN RIGHTS
- SOCI 302 WOMEN AND GLOBAL POVERTY or SOCI 361 GENDER, WORK, AND FAMILY
- SOCI 304 GLOBALIZATION AND SOCIETY
- SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS
- SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY
- SOCI 317 SOCIOLOGY OF COMMUNITY: FIELDWORK
- SOCI 332 SOCIAL THEORY
- SOCI 410 CAPSTONE PROJECT IN SOCIOLOGY

SOCI 101 is 4 credits; no prerequisites are published. [2] SOCI 308 is 4 credits; its prerequisite is SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS, which may be taken concurrently. [3] SOCI 410 is 4 credits; prerequisites are CRWT 102 CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II or CRWT 102S CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II; SOCI 101 INTRODUCTION TO SOCIOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY; SOCI 317 SOCIOLOGY OF COMMUNITY: FIELDWORK; and SOCI 332 SOCIAL THEORY. SOCI 308, 317, and 332 may be taken concurrently with SOCI 410. [5]

SOCI 335 PUBLIC SOCIOLOGIES is an option among the Social Inequality concentration electives, not a required course by itself. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-SOCI) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/SOCI101) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/SOCI308) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/SOCI410) [18](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: Can a course count toward both my major and a minor at the same time, or is there a limit on how many credits can overlap?
answer:
Yes. Courses required for your primary or secondary major may count toward your minor, but no more than half of the minor credits may overlap [2].

question: what does psyc 101 cover and how many credits is it? also is it a prereq for research methods
answer:
PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology is 4 credits. It introduces psychology as a field of study and practice, exploring its history, methods and scope. Topics include learning, perception, cognition, emotion, motivation, abnormal behavior, psychotherapy, social behavior, personality, development across the lifespan, and biological bases of thought, feeling and action. [1]

Yes. PSYC 101 is a prerequisite for PSYC 303 Research Methods in Psychology (4 credits). PSYC 303 also requires CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S, and PSYC 242 or BADM 225; the catalog lists all three prerequisite requirements. [2]

question: what's the total number of credits needed to graduate from Ramapo and is there a minimum number I have to take at Ramapo itself as a transfer?
answer:
For an undergraduate degree, the minimum is 128 credits that count toward graduation; some programs may require more [3, 4, 6, 7, 8]. As a transfer, the minimum to complete at Ramapo depends on where you transfer from: at least 63 credits if entering from a two-year college, or at least 32 if entering from a four-year college [4].

The pages differ on the general Ramapo residency minimum: sections 1, 3, 7 and 8 say 32 credits at Ramapo, while section 6 says 48 [1, 3, 6, 7, 8]. Section 1 also requires your final 32 credits at Ramapo or in a Ramapo-approved study abroad program or experience, and at least half the requirements of your major, second major or minor at Ramapo [1]. Section 3 says the final 32 credits must be completed in residence and at least half the credits for your primary major, second major and minor(s) at Ramapo [3]. Section 6 likewise requires the final 32 in residence and at least half the credits for majors/second majors/minors at Ramapo [6].

Check your applicable Catalog and major/program requirements; specific programs may require additional credits [3, 4]. For clarification, contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695 [6].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#undergraduate-residency-requirement1) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#graduation-requirements) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/)

question: Should I do a double major in poli sci and history or just add a minor? I only have 4 semesters left and want to graduate on time
answer:
I can’t recommend one option or verify that you can graduate on time from these pages; that depends on your degree audit and remaining requirements. For a double major, no more than half the courses may count toward both majors, and you must complete all writing-intensive courses required for the second major [7]. A minor must include 16–24 credits; courses may overlap with a major, but no more than half the minor credits may overlap [6].

To assess your timeline, review your Degree Audit, then make an appointment with your faculty academic advisor about remaining graduation courses [8]. If you are a senior, the guidance says to have 128 credits before beginning your final semester [9]. It also recommends at least 16 credit hours each semester to be in position to graduate on time [10].
